::: {#sol-overfit-curves}

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Training and validation loss on a log scale against epoch, over 300 epochs.
#|   The training loss falls steadily toward 0.
#|   The validation loss falls to a minimum early in training and then rises.
plain_net = make_net()
plain_history, plain_best_state = fit(plain_net)
best_row = plain_history.loc[plain_history["val"].idxmin()]
best_epoch = int(best_row["epoch"])
best_val_loss = best_row["val"]
final_row = plain_history.iloc[-1]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3.5), layout="constrained")
ax.plot(plain_history["epoch"], plain_history["train"], label="training");
ax.plot(plain_history["epoch"], plain_history["val"], label="validation");
ax.axvline(best_epoch, color="gray", linestyle=":");
ax.set_yscale("log");
ax.set_xlabel("epoch");
ax.set_ylabel("cross-entropy loss");
ax.legend();
plt.show()
print(best_epoch, best_val_loss, final_row["train"], final_row["val"])
```

The training loss falls the whole time,
to `r sprintf("%.1e", py$final_row[["train"]])` after 300 [epochs](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/gradient-descent.html#def-epoch).
The validation loss falls to its lowest value,
`r sprintf("%.3f", py$best_val_loss)`,
at [epoch](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/gradient-descent.html#def-epoch) `r py$best_epoch`,
marked by the dotted line,
and then rises to `r sprintf("%.3f", py$final_row[["val"]])`.
After epoch `r py$best_epoch` the network goes on fitting the training images
in ways that do not carry over to new images:
it [overfits](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/big-ideas.html#def-overfitting).

:::
